solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Apartment assigned to sailor, sort of plain?

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor, so SALT stands for him
a flat is the British word for an apartment

explanation.surface: A seaman is given an apartment, and the question is what kind of plain place that is.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs in answer order, sailor first, even though the clue mentions the apartment first; 'assigned to' just links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt flat is a level expanse of crusted salt left by evaporated water, one kind of flat open terrain.

clue.text: In section of Harare, national stadium

indicators.note: In section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sporting venue in part of Zimbabwe's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or entertainment, a stadium by another name.

clue.text: A trip tutors arranged brings one to a place that exploits visitors

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teachers organise an outing that lands them somewhere overpriced.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist trap is a spot that overcharges sightseers for what it offers.

clue.text: Catch post in location near Penzance

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: A fishing catch is mailed from somewhere in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, a few miles from the Cornish town of Penzance.

clue.text: Act quixotically seeing charge applied to children's toys?

parts.note: to tilt at someone is to charge at them with a lance
windmills are toy pinwheels that spin in the wind

explanation.surface: Behaving like Don Quixote, when one sees an attack on playthings.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote charged at windmills thinking they were giants, hence the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To tilt at windmills is to fight imaginary enemies, the hopeless idealism named after Cervantes's hero.

clue.text: Quick on the uptake, like famous pharaoh, leader of Egyptians

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of 'in the manner of'
Tut, short for Tutankhamun, the best-known pharaoh

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so the first of Egyptians is taken

explanation.surface: Someone sharp-witted is likened to Tutankhamun, head of the Egyptians.
explanation.definitionFit: An astute person is shrewd and grasps things quickly, which is what being quick on the uptake describes.

clue.text: A dishonourable man splitting note in shopping precinct

indicators.note: splitting means going between the letters of the note, separating them

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A scoundrel causes a rift over a banknote in the mall.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered passage lined with shops, a kind of shopping precinct.

clue.text: Trial judge

definitions.meaning: to ... a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: A court hearing and its presiding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Try covers both an attempt and hearing a case in court, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Incorrectly spelt rice liqueur

indicators.note: incorrectly suggests the letters are in the wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone has misspelt the name of a rice liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is a clear orange-flavoured liqueur used in cocktails.

clue.text: Elect to go back

definitions.meaning: a constituency ... a candidate when it elects them to parliament
to come or go back to a place

explanation.surface: Choosing to head home again.
explanation.definitionFit: Return covers both voting someone into office and travelling back somewhere, two separate senses of one verb.

clue.text: Duly pick off game

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Duly choosing to call off a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of the phrase 'pick off', but it is the anagram signal working on DULY PICK. A lucky dip is a British fairground game: you pull an unseen prize from a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip is a game of chance in which a hidden prize is drawn at random.

clue.text: Cab charge beginning to irk

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied by government

indicators.note: beginning to a word means its opening letter, here of irk

explanation.surface: A taxi fare that starts to annoy the passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: Cab is the everyday short name for a taxi, a car hired with its driver.

clue.text: Stop to pay for another photograph

parts.note: to stand someone a drink or meal is to pay for it on their behalf
a still is a single photograph, especially one taken from a film

explanation.surface: A pause to pay for a second picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' seems to mean a second photograph, but it belongs with 'pay for': to stand another person something is to treat them.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a complete halt, when everything stops moving.

clue.text: Incredible shows to watch across a city in Florida

indicators.note: across means the other pieces stretch over the a, which sits within them

parts.note: a tall story is an incredible one
has, as in a gallery that has (shows) a painting
to see is to watch

explanation.surface: Amazing performances to watch throughout a Florida city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' as HAS is the stretch: a gallery that has a painting shows it. 'across' has the other pieces span the lone a.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallahassee is the state capital of Florida.

clue.text: Question, perhaps asked when greeting wife, was then outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wild, unruly behaviour, so the letters of was then are scrambled

explanation.surface: Greeting one's wife with a question that turned out shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: 'What's new?' is the casual enquiry people make on meeting a friend, asking for their latest news.

clue.text: Casserole at last in bistro? Controversial issue

parts.note: hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat topped with sliced potato

indicators.note: last in a word means its final letter, here of bistro

explanation.surface: Finally a stew on the menu at a bistro.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire hotpot is a British slow-cooked lamb casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is a contentious matter that people prefer not to handle.

clue.text: Survive piece of strong criticism? Not bishop

indicators.note: Not here tells us to leave out the named letter, the bishop

parts.note: a blast is a furious outburst of criticism
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Enduring a harsh rebuke, unless one is a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bishop' takes B out of BLAST.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to keep going or endure, which is what surviving means.

clue.text: Curry and plonk old boy served up inside

indicators.note: inside places the reversed old boy within the wine

parts.note: plonk is cheap wine, vino informally

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A curry and cheap wine are brought to an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns OLAD into DALO, and 'inside' puts it within VINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiery curry from Goa.

clue.text: Celebrity's brief introduction

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a start is the beginning or introduction of something

explanation.surface: A famous person's short opening remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the final T from START.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, the sort of person called a celebrity.

clue.text: Pest is hidden by shade

indicators.note: something hidden by another is enclosed inside it, so is goes within the shade word

parts.note: a nuance is a slight shade of meaning or colour

explanation.surface: An insect lurks concealed in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoying person or thing, which is what a pest is in everyday speech.

clue.text: Where there may be some work to do?

definitions.text: Where there may be some work to do?

parts.words: Where there may be some work to do?
parts.note: describes the desk tray holding papers still to be dealt with

explanation.surface: Asking where some pending tasks might be found.
explanation.definitionFit: An office tray holds incoming documents awaiting attention, so jobs to be done sit there.

clue.text: In a frightful rage, nail GM a day after dance

indicators.note: after places the dance word before what follows it, setting the order

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
a pin is a small slender nail

explanation.surface: Someone livid, nailing General Motors a day after a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping mad is an idiom for being furiously angry, as if jumping with rage.

clue.text: American girl, short, I'm sorry to say

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A brief apology to a petite American girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last S from LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of regret, used where one might say 'unfortunately'.

clue.text: Farewell to the Parisian about to depart

definitions.text: Farewell to the Parisian about to depart

parts.words: Farewell to the Parisian about to depart
parts.note: the goodbye a French speaker says when leaving

explanation.surface: A goodbye said to someone from Paris on the point of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French word for goodbye, literally commending someone to God.

clue.text: Skin cream said to come from a highland castle

parts.note: a balm is a soothing ointment for the skin
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A moisturiser claimed to originate from a Scottish castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Unruly bunch kept in Guantanamo Bay

indicators.note: kept in says the letters are held within the place name that follows

explanation.surface: A disorderly group detained at the US base in Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob is a disorderly crowd of people.

clue.text: Off course, Italian gave way to violent anger

parts.note: a traveller who is off course is lost
It is an abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian strayed off course and then flew into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost it is an informal idiom for losing one's temper completely.

clue.text: Intimidate by circling round drover

parts.note: to cow someone is to frighten them into submission

indicators.note: circling means going around something, so by goes round the ring letter

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Bullying someone by riding in circles, as a cattle drover might.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy herds cattle on horseback, the American counterpart of a drover.

clue.text: Appeared embarrassed

definitions.meaning: to show someone up is to humiliate them in public

explanation.surface: Turned up looking awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both turning up somewhere and making someone look foolish, two distinct senses.
